dead_ends.why_failed: git does not track mtimes; clones equalize them and attackers forge them - v1.12.0 chained to the wrong predecessor with check still passing

dead_ends.approach: existence-only checks for council verdict and sign-offs
dead_ends.why_failed: empty files satisfy existence; 'no verdict, no gold' must mean bytes, so hashedref content-pinning replaced it

learned.claim: v0.4.0: opt-in enterprise profile - Merge Council (unanimity), permission matrix, Gold Build ladder; doctrine_gold check is the deploy gate and the hash chain is the rollback ladder.
Existence is not evidence: zero-byte sign-off files satisfied the v1 gate. Verdict and sign-offs are now content-pinned (path+sha256) and re-hashed at deploy.
mtime is never an authority signal: clone-reset/forged mtimes forked the gold chain silently. Order now derives only from prev-hash links (one genesis, no forks, full reachability).
Fail-closed topology: a broken gold ladder blocks ALL deploys until repaired, not just the suspect record - confirmed as correct posture by the code reviewer.
Both lessons promoted to doctrine: backend.md content-hash-references bullet joins the transactional-artifacts rule from round 1.

next_actions: Wire doctrine_gold check into a real deploy pipeline when this repo (or a consumer) gains one
